system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:37:57, ben.carter's interactive session launched cmupdate.exe from the user's AppData\Local\ChartMate directory at medium integrity, rather than the approved Program Files location described in the inventory.

The updater process made repeated outbound proxy connections to update.chartmate-imaging.net, while the inventory identifies update.chartmate-imaging.com as the approved ChartMate update host. The observed hostname differs from the approved hostname.

Connections to the .net hostname recur at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:38 through 14:08. Successful requests have similar tunnel byte counts, and some attempts returned proxy errors; this pattern is consistent with periodic check-in activity.

While running, cmupdate.exe generated a file-creation event targeting its own executable path. This is compatible with self-update behavior but, given the unusual path and hostname, adds to the concern and is not independently proof of maliciousness.

WS-BCARTER-01 connected to FILE-HD-01 over SMB, and FILE-HD-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon. This is unexplained in the supplied evidence; the records do not show what share or files, if any, were accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The stated winsec and Sysmon collection outage applies to WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, not WS-BCARTER-01; the supplied coverage status marks the other hosts and times as operational.
The successful HTTPS records are proxy CONNECT tunnels and provide host, byte counts, and duration, not the encrypted request contents or destination URL paths.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the executable's hash, signature, provenance, or whether it is genuinely a ChartMate component.
The evidence does not establish the content or purpose of the HTTPS traffic, or that data was exfiltrated.
The SMB records do not establish successful access to any share, file reads or writes, or the reason for the anonymous logon.
The evidence does not identify who installed or introduced the executable, or establish persistence or a broader compromise.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire cmupdate.exe and determine its hash, Authenticode signature, file metadata, and provenance; compare it with a trusted ChartMate installer and approved installation.
Review endpoint file, process, persistence, and download history for the executable and its parent process.
Obtain DNS and TLS details for update.chartmate-imaging.net, including resolved addresses, certificate information, and reputation; inspect decrypted proxy content if available.
Review FILE-HD-01 share-access and object-access auditing around 13:54 UTC to determine whether any resources were accessed.
Check whether the same executable, hostname, or connection pattern appears on other hosts.
